description: CityBES is a web-based data and computing platform from Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory for energy modelling of a city's building stock, supporting district and city efficiency programmes. It represents buildings with CityGML, simulates energy use and retrofit savings with EnergyPlus through the CBES SDK built on OpenStudio, and won a 2022 R&D 100 Award. Its data layer combines weather, 3D city models built from GIS, land use and assessor records, and databases of efficiency measures, utility rates and codes. Use cases include benchmarking, retrofit analysis, district heating and cooling modelling with load profiles from the DOE prototype and reference buildings, renewable energy, heat resilience, and census-tract mapping of microclimate and heat vulnerability. Coverage: city stocks prepared by users; the data notes list U.S. city coordinate systems such as San Francisco, Los Angeles, New York and Portland. Access: account sign-in. Licence: not stated. Caveats: results depend on the quality of assessor and GIS inputs, and access is by account. Simulation uses: city-scale retrofit, electrification and heat resilience scenarios. Related records: EnergyPlus, OpenStudio and the DOE prototype building models.
